candidates.explanation: The capability core is cohesive, with justified Next.js and job runtime entries. It defines a framework-neutral shared operation and provider-owned port, uses a Route Handler with propagated cancellation and resettable idle timing, distinguishes pre/post-commit failures, preserves separate HTTP/SSE/job contracts, and prevents provider details or SDK types from leaking.

The design is spread across generic domain, ports, use-cases, boundary, adapters, and infrastructure roots, with two route-related locations, so it is not colocated under one capability root. Otherwise it provides a provider-neutral shared operation and port, correct Route Handler/SSE lifecycle, channel-specific failure handling and job decisions, and no provider-type leakage.

Assistant behavior is scattered across app, ui, domain, application, infrastructure, lib, and tests rather than one capability root. The remaining design is coherent: a framework-neutral use case and capability port, propagated abort with per-read idle timeout, commit-aware SSE failures, distinct job retry/dead-letter semantics, shared safe classification/reporting, and isolated provider types.

The proposal cleanly owns behavior under one assistant module with only the App Router entry outside it. Its application operation and provider port are framework-neutral and capability-shaped; the stream boundary correctly handles abort, idle timeout, commitment, safe mapping, and once-only reporting; the job retains native retry/dead-letter behavior; and provider protocol, messages, and types remain private.
